A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with SMACS renamed SMCS. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, tables, and figures can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original eight-benchmark evaluations, scaling experiments, component ablations, aggregator comparisons, and longer-output experiments, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds original efficiency, out-of-distribution, repeated-seed, perplexity, and cost-versus-accuracy experiments.

M1.justification: Despite the SMACS-to-SMCS rename, Section 3 retains the unified question bank, similarity-weighted model selection, prior-based dropping, repeated aggregation, and hybrid similarity/perplexity scoring. No new algorithmic component or changed inference procedure is established.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original eight benchmarks and adds HumanEval, FinQA, and LiveMathBench as unseen-benchmark evaluations using the existing question bank (Appendix A.6). Section 4.5 also introduces a distinct retrieval-transfer scenario: an MMLU-PRO-only bank supporting evaluation on AIME, MBPP, GPQA-Diamond, and MedMCQA.

E2.justification: The new question-bank comparison includes an evaluated random-selection control without a question bank (v2 Table 3). Table 1 retains the same six collaboration baselines and individual LLMs. Newly discussed GraphRouter and MODEL-SAT are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds restricted-bank and unseen-benchmark evaluation protocols, API cost and latency measurements, and MMLU-PRO sweeps over referencer count, aggregation count, and retrieval-bank support size. Appendix A.3 also changes the stated embedding dimension from 4,096 to 8,192; this documents a setting revision without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test retrieval under distribution mismatch, the numerical scale of perplexity, and accuracy/cost sensitivity to three hyperparameters (Section 4.5 and Appendices A.6, A.7, A.10). The original component ablation is retained unchanged, moving from v1 Section 4.4/Table 2 to v2 Appendix A.9/Table 10.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports three runs with different random seeds and mean/standard-deviation results for SMCS and three comparators across four datasets (Appendix A.8, Table 9). Table 8 also adds perplexity distribution summaries. v1 provides no corresponding repeated-run or uncertainty reporting; v2 does not add formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Shared scores in the main and longer-output tables remain unchanged, including system averages of 76.78 and 81.01. v2 adds substantial results, including 95.12 on HumanEval, 75.24 on FinQA, and 74.38 on LiveMathBench (Table 7), plus cost/latency, repeated-seed, perplexity, and budget-sweep results. Closed-source upper-bound summary rows are removed.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(8), including the selection, sampling, scoring, and ranking definitions, are retained. Appendix A.7 discusses the existing perplexity score's numerical scale and empirical behavior without introducing a substantive new formal definition, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The main narrative removes the claim of exceeding the closed-source per-dataset upper-bound average by 2.04 points, while retaining the scalable collaboration contribution and comparisons with GPT models and open-source best results. The longer-output closed-source upper-bound claim remains in Appendix A.5, so it is not removed throughout the paper.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning inexpensive APIs and parallel inference, generalization supported by question-bank diversity, prospective online bank expansion, perplexity normalization, and budget trade-offs. These substantially expand the discussion of mechanisms and applicability. The original limitations concerning computational resources and uniform inference configurations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 revises the embedding dimension and newly specifies eight responses for Self-MoA, while most generation settings and the supplied prompts remain unchanged. The abstract changes a promised code release into a stated release at the renamed SMCS repository.

R1.justification: Related work adds GraphRouter and MODEL-SAT, expands the RouterDC discussion, and places MoA and Self-MoA under posterior collaboration. Some general NLP and repeated-sampling background is removed, and references supporting the new benchmarks are added. The central prior-versus-posterior positioning remains.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, the abstract is rewritten, and the introduction and related-work narrative are substantially recast around multi-LLM collaboration. Terminology changes throughout from SMACS/MACS to SMCS/MCS. The experimental narrative is reorganized, including moving component ablations into the appendix and shortening the conclusion.

P2.justification: v2 adds the conceptual comparison diagram in Figure 2 and eight tables covering efficiency, distribution mismatch, perplexity, uncertainty, and budget sweeps. Existing displays are relocated and relabeled, including the component-ablation table. The main results table also changes its highlighted comparison rows and removes the closed-source upper-bound row.

improvement.justification: The new unseen-benchmark evaluations, three-seed results, and cost/latency and budget analyses address important gaps in v1's evidence for generalization, reliability, and practical scalability. They substantially strengthen the empirical case while preserving the original results. Some new interpretations overreach the evidence, particularly treating perplexity summaries as strict bounds, but these weaknesses do not outweigh the added direct experimental support.
